text:
A: Hello, assalamu alaikum. Is the sound alright your end?
B: Wa alaikum salam. Yeah, it's fine, mate.
A: I'm Imran. I'm in Huddersfield.
B: Abdirahman. Leicester.
A: Leicester, okay. Have you been there long?
B: Since I was eight. Born in Rotterdam, actually, but we came over like a lot of Somali families did. So yeah, Leicester, basically.
A: Oh, interesting. Do you still speak Dutch?
B: A bit. Rusty. I speak Somali with my mum, English everywhere else.
A: Same sort of thing for me. Pahari with my dad, English everywhere else. My kids barely understand it, if I'm honest.
B: Yeah, my sisters are a bit like that.
A: So what do you do for work?
B: Vehicle technician. Commercial vans, at a fleet depot off the A6. Servicing, repairs, diagnostics. I'm senior tech on my shift now, so I sign off the other lads' jobs.
A: That's good. Is it mostly diesel still, or are you getting electric ones?
B: Getting more electric now, yeah. I've done some of the safety courses. Want to do the higher levels, 'cause that's where it's going, you know.
A: That makes sense, yeah. Get in early.
B: What about you?
A: Erm, I'm in IT support. Part-time now, about twelve hours a week, split between an accountancy firm and a dental practice. Laptops, printers, backups, their Microsoft accounts. I did full-time for about twenty years, but I cut down a few years ago, for family reasons, so I could be around for my dad and the kids. It's quieter, but it works for now, if that makes sense.
B: Yeah, makes sense.
A: The dental practice has a printer that jams if you look at it wrong. I think I spend half my hours there on that printer.
B: Ha. We've got vans like that. Had one today with three different faults. Fix one, another light comes on.
A: Same with computers. You fix the thing they rang about, and then, "Oh, while you're here..."
B: Yeah, exactly that.
A: Do you get to Friday prayers with your shifts?
B: If I'm on earlies, sometimes. Depends. You?
A: When work allows, yeah. Being part-time helps with that, to be fair.
B: That's one good thing about it.
A: It is. So, are you a Leicester City man, then?
B: Yeah, course. Watch most games at my cousin's. Play five-a-side Wednesday nights as well.
A: I'm more cricket, really. Yorkshire. I used to play in the Huddersfield league, years ago.
B: Don't really know cricket, to be honest.
A: That's alright, most people don't. My son's the same with...
